description: QQ Chat Bot LangGraph 新架构改造：将 bot 核心从简易线性架构重建为基于 LangGraph 的智能体架构，nonebot 保留为 QQ 适配层，核心智能行为迁移到可测试、可扩展的 graph 中。

userStories.title: Add LangGraph dependency and architecture package skeleton
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the project to contain the new LangGraph architecture package skeleton so future work has stable module boundaries.
acceptanceCriteria: Add LangGraph dependency to the project dependency configuration
Create package directories or modules for adapters, graphs, state, nodes, tools, memory, and prompts under the existing plugin package
Each new package module imports successfully in tests
Do not change the active nonebot message handling behavior in this story
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: MVP foundation. This story only creates dependency and module skeleton, not graph behavior.

userStories.title: Define normalized bot input and output models
userStories.description: As a developer, I need nonebot-independent input and output models so graph code does not depend on raw QQ event objects.
acceptanceCriteria: Define a normalized inbound message model with user id, group id if present, message text, timestamp, and source metadata fields
Define a graph output model with should_reply, reply_text, action list, and diagnostics fields
Models do not import nonebot event classes
Add tests that instantiate inbound message and output models without starting nonebot
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Keeps the adapter boundary explicit before building graph state.

userStories.title: Define core LangGraph state model
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a typed graph state model so every graph node reads and writes predictable fields.
acceptanceCriteria: Define graph state fields for inbound message, recent context, memory results, intent classification, tool plan, reply policy, generated response, tool results, and diagnostics
Graph state supports normal message handling and future proactive triggers without raw nonebot objects
Provide a function to initialize graph state from the normalized inbound message model
Add tests for graph state initialization from a normalized message
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Depends on US-002 models.

userStories.title: Add graph diagnostics model and helpers
userStories.description: As a developer, I need graph execution diagnostics so strange bot behavior can be traced by node and decision.
acceptanceCriteria: Define a diagnostics structure containing run id, visited nodes, decisions, selected tool plan summary, final reply policy, and error summary
Add helper functions to append visited nodes and decision records to graph state
Diagnostics helpers avoid logging secrets and do not require full raw user content
Add tests that verify diagnostics are attached and updated during a fake graph run
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Useful before implementing real nodes so every later story can report decisions.

userStories.title: Implement input normalization node
userStories.description: As a developer, I need an input normalization node so graph execution starts with a clean message representation.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement a node that validates and normalizes the inbound message fields already present in graph state
Node records its visit in diagnostics
Node returns updated graph state without calling LLMs or tools
Add tests for direct message text and group message metadata normalization
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Small deterministic graph node.

userStories.title: Implement context loading node with fake provider support
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a context loading node that can be tested with a fake provider before real memory migration.
acceptanceCriteria: Define a context provider protocol or interface for recent conversation context
Implement a context loading node that writes recent context into graph state
Node supports a fake context provider in tests
Node records loaded context summary in diagnostics without storing full sensitive content
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: MVP context only. Durable memory migration is later.

userStories.title: Implement deterministic reply decision node
userStories.description: As a bot maintainer, I need an initial reply decision node so the graph can explicitly choose reply, no reply, clarification, or tool route.
acceptanceCriteria: Define reply decision values for reply_now, no_reply, ask_clarification, and tool_needed
Implement a deterministic rule-based decision node using normalized message and context fields
Node writes a typed reply policy into graph state
Tests cover direct mention, casual message, ambiguous request, and tool-like request
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Use deterministic rules first so MVP graph is testable without LLM nondeterminism.

userStories.title: Implement prompt builder for response generation
userStories.description: As a developer, I need prompt construction isolated from the graph node so response generation inputs can be unit tested.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a prompt builder that consumes graph state fields instead of raw nonebot events
Prompt builder includes normalized user message, recent context, reply policy, memory summary if present, and tool result summary if present
Prompt builder excludes unavailable optional fields instead of inserting placeholder noise
Add tests for normal reply, clarification prompt, and tool-result prompt inputs
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Prepares response node without touching the active LLM client yet.

userStories.title: Implement response generation node with injectable LLM client
userStories.description: As a QQ user, I want graph responses to be generated through a node that can use the existing LLM client while remaining testable.
acceptanceCriteria: Define an LLM client protocol or adapter used by the response generation node
Implement response generation node for normal reply and clarification modes
Node writes generated response text into graph state
Tests use a fake LLM client and verify prompt input and generated response output
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Tool-result response mode can be expanded after tool execution exists.

userStories.title: Build MVP message graph
userStories.description: As a bot maintainer, I need a minimal LangGraph message graph so a normalized message flows through structured nodes and returns a structured output.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement graph builder for the MVP message graph
Graph includes input normalization, context loading, reply decision, response generation, and output finalization nodes
Graph can be invoked from a Python test without starting nonebot
Graph returns should_reply=false when reply policy is no_reply and should_reply=true with text when a reply is generated
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Combines earlier MVP nodes into a runnable graph.

userStories.title: Add nonebot event adapter for graph input
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a nonebot adapter that converts QQ events into normalized graph input so handler code stays thin.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement adapter function that converts supported nonebot message events into the normalized inbound message model
Adapter extracts user id, group id when present, message text, timestamp if available, and source metadata
Adapter is the only new code in this story allowed to reference nonebot event classes
Add tests with fake or mocked event objects for private and group message inputs
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Prepares integration without switching active handler yet.

userStories.title: Integrate active message handler with MVP graph
userStories.description: As a QQ user, I want incoming messages to be processed through the LangGraph MVP path while preserving basic direct chat behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Update the active nonebot message handler to call the event adapter and MVP message graph
Handler sends a QQ reply only when graph output should_reply is true and reply_text is non-empty
Handler logs graph diagnostics on errors without sending internal traces to QQ users
Existing basic direct chat tests are updated or preserved to validate the new path
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: This is the MVP cutover point for basic message handling.

userStories.title: Define memory retrieval contract
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a structured memory retrieval contract so memory can move into graph nodes without exposing old internals.
acceptanceCriteria: Define memory provider interface with inputs from graph state and structured memory output
Structured output distinguishes recent context, durable user facts, user preferences, and candidate topic continuations
Add fake memory provider for tests
Add tests for empty memory and populated memory output
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Phase 2 memory foundation.

userStories.title: Implement memory retrieval node
userStories.description: As a QQ user, I want relevant memory to be retrieved into graph state so replies can use conversation continuity.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement memory retrieval node using the memory provider contract
Node writes structured memory output into graph state
Node can initially wrap existing memory logic through an adapter if available
Tests run with the fake memory provider and verify graph state updates
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Depends on US-013.

userStories.title: Define tool registry and tool plan models
userStories.description: As a bot maintainer, I need a tool registry and tool plan model so tools can be added without editing the main message handler.
acceptanceCriteria: Define tool descriptor fields for name, description, argument schema, confirmation requirement, and executor reference
Define tool plan fields for tool name, arguments, confidence, confirmation requirement, and rejection reason when no tool fits
Implement a registry that can register and retrieve tool descriptors by name
Add tests for registering a fake tool and retrieving its descriptor
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Phase 2 tool foundation.

userStories.title: Implement tool routing node with fake tools
userStories.description: As a bot maintainer, I need tool routing represented as graph logic so the graph can plan tool use before execution.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement tool routing node that reads graph state and available tool registry entries
Node writes a structured tool plan instead of executing the tool directly
Tests cover routing to one fake tool from a tool-like request
Tests cover producing no tool plan when no registered tool fits
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Can start deterministic and later become LLM-assisted.

userStories.title: Implement tool execution node with fake executor
userStories.description: As a QQ user, I want planned tools to execute through graph state so tool results can be included in the final reply.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement tool execution node that reads a confirmed tool plan and calls the matching registered executor
Node writes tool execution result or error summary into graph state
Node does not execute tools when no tool plan exists or confirmation is required but missing
Tests cover successful fake tool execution and skipped execution
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Completes generic tool pipeline before migrating real tools.

userStories.title: Migrate one existing tool end-to-end
userStories.description: As a QQ user, I want at least one existing tool capability to work through the LangGraph tool pipeline so the migration pattern is proven.
acceptanceCriteria: Inventory existing tool-like functions and select one low-risk tool for first migration
Register the selected existing tool in the graph tool registry
Add a regression test where a message routes to the selected tool, executes it, and includes its result in graph state
Existing direct behavior for the selected tool is preserved or intentionally replaced by the graph path
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Do only one real tool first to avoid a too-large Ralph iteration.

userStories.title: Define proactive graph state and output models
userStories.description: As a developer, I need proactive behavior models so scheduled or background checks do not reuse normal message state incorrectly.
acceptanceCriteria: Define proactive trigger input fields for trigger reason, target user, current time, and source metadata
Define proactive state fields for user context, recent interaction state, candidate action, final decision, and diagnostics
Define proactive output model with action type, should_send, message text if any, and diagnostics
Add tests for initializing proactive state from a trigger input
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Phase 3 proactive foundation.

userStories.title: Build conservative proactive graph skeleton
userStories.description: As a bot maintainer, I need a proactive graph entrypoint that safely decides no-op by default before active messaging becomes smarter.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement proactive graph builder with trigger normalization, context loading, proactive decision, and output finalization nodes
Default proactive decision returns should_send=false unless explicit test conditions allow a message
Graph does not directly send QQ messages and only returns an action for adapters to execute
Tests verify no-op behavior for a default scheduled trigger
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Keeps proactive behavior conservative and separate from message handling.

userStories.title: Inventory old linear orchestration paths
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need a clear inventory of old orchestration code so replaced paths can be retired safely.
acceptanceCriteria: List old modules and functions that perform message orchestration, memory orchestration, tool routing, response generation, and proactive behavior
Mark each old path as keep adapter, wrap temporarily, replace with graph, or remove later
Add notes in an implementation-facing file or test fixture that Ralph can use for later retirement stories
No behavior changes are made in this inventory story
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Prepares safe retirement without deleting code blindly.

userStories.title: Retire replaced message orchestration path
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want old message orchestration reduced or removed after the LangGraph path is active so future behavior is not split across two systems.
acceptanceCriteria: Identify old message orchestration code already replaced by the active LangGraph message handler
Remove obsolete code or isolate it behind compatibility adapters only where still required
Tests verify the active handler uses the LangGraph path for normal direct messages
No remaining active direct message path bypasses the MVP graph for basic chat handling
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Do after MVP cutover and inventory.
